o1.biggest_strength: Copy is genuinely in our voice — short, calm lines like 'Land. Roll. Leave.' — and it turns quiet wheels, belt-skipping and lift-it-alone into three separate shootable concepts with hooks pulled from real review lines.
o1.biggest_mistake: Its test plan is too thin to judge anything: three times blended cost per purchase is about ₹4,500, roughly three purchases per concept, and running a women-specific concept inside one broad campaign muddles the very read it is asking for.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Set a real sample per concept (15+ purchases), pair it with a proper budget, and name the 85 scuff reviews and the 60 front-pocket requests up front so the team knows what not to shoot.

o2.biggest_strength: It leads with the two awkward truths in my data — scuffs on dark shells and the missing front pocket — then hands my team sizes, safe zones, CTA, link, paid-partnership labelling, character-counted headlines and a ₹63,000 test budget with a 15-purchase rule.
o2.biggest_mistake: Primary texts drift into spec-listing, so a few read denser than our 'short lines, grade 7' voice, and showing a real luggage-scale reading risks displaying a number that disagrees with 'about 2.6 kg'.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten every primary text to our calm short-line rhythm and make the weight demo a craft shot or a scripted 'about 2.6 kg' rather than an unscripted scale reading.

reason: Output 2 tells me about the scuff and front-pocket problem before I shoot, and gives sizes, safe zones, labels and a ₹63,000 test with a 15-purchase rule, so the team can run it and I can trust the read; Output 1's copy is a touch calmer, but its ₹4,500-per-concept test is barely three purchases.
